lede: The profile page is over four screens long, sign out is at the very bottom, and nothing a child does in a game changes how they look to anyone else. This plan tidies the page, swaps levels for trophies that last, and makes the hardest feats in every game win a painted profile picture, with a typed name as the top prize.

findings.title: Too long, and sign out is last
findings.text: On a Chromebook the page is 3,219 px tall with 71 things to tap. The child's own avatar is two screens down and Sign out is the last thing on the page.

findings.title: Levels: retire them
findings.text: 100 of 162 pupils are level 1 and one has reached level 7. A level unlocks nothing, classmates never see it, the early-years games give no points, and it is wiped each year. Keep points for "points this week"; let trophies replace the level bar.

findings.title: Achievements are a list, not a reward
findings.text: 196 kinds across 27 games, shown all at once as an emoji and a name. 115 pupils have at least one; the most is 49. None is visible to classmates.

findings.title: Nothing lasts
findings.text: The yearly New Season wipes most game records. Trophies need their own table that it never touches, written at the moment of the feat.

findings.title: One season for the whole hub
findings.text: The hub gets its own season clock that you set (35 days to start, and you can pause it). Every game's trophies use it. Dragon Maths trophies follow the dragon's own season: season 1 ends about 21 November, and its five slayers get the first bronze Dragon Heads.

findings.title: Bronze, silver, gold
findings.text: Win a trophy in one season for bronze, a second season for silver, a third for gold. That is the reward for coming back. The hardest feat in each game also unlocks a painted profile picture.

findings.title: A typed name needs a teacher's Yes
findings.text: The privacy summary promises no free typing. An earned name is fine if nobody sees it until a teacher approves it, the server checks for rude words, and the summary gets one new line.

findings.title: The best rewards need two games
findings.text: Seven rewards need a feat in two different games, such as slaying the dragon and beating the clan monster in one season. The Name Scroll needs gold trophies in two different games. This pushes pupils to vary their play.

findings.title: Fair for the youngest
findings.text: Early-years rewards come from days played and prizes finished: the game's painted friends become profile pictures. No races, no speed, no maths levels on show.

recs.done: Avatar, name and Sign out are on the first screen. Everything else is behind closed folds or a "Change my look" button.
recs.why: Every child signs out of a shared Chromebook every lesson. It should take one tap.
